pointer_operability_surface_label: Example State official voter-information pointer-operability fail-open policy
delivery_role_note: Critical official voter-information routes remain reachable with ordinary touch or coarse-pointer input and do not depend on tiny targets, hover-only reveals, or gesture-only interaction to expose the current answer.
target_size_and_spacing_note: Critical controls in the answer/help lane expose adequately sized or sufficiently separated activation areas for ordinary touch and coarse-pointer use.
hover_revealed_content_note: Hover-triggered disclosures are not the only place where deadline, warning, office-hour, or next-step meaning lives; equivalent no-hover content remains reachable.
single_point_alternative_note: Path-based or multi-step pointer gestures that affect the answer lane have a simple tap/select/list alternative.
coarse_pointer_adaptation_note: Routes behave coherently when the primary input cannot hover or is not highly accurate, without silently changing the authoritative answer.
map_pin_and_dense_control_note: Map pins, chips, tabs, close icons, and other dense controls affecting the answer lane are backed by a readable list/text or otherwise remain realistically activatable.
dismiss_and_close_control_note: Dismiss, close, next-step, and help controls remain easy to hit and do not collapse into tiny precision-only targets.
same_answer_across_pointer_variants_note: Touch-first, coarse-pointer, and no-hover variants may change presentation but do not silently change the authoritative answer.
manual_help_contact_note: A plainly visible first-party help/contact lane remains available when the main route becomes pointer-hostile or fiddly.
